https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live.text: Ove 60 percent of prospective voters in Michigan, a border state both heavily dependent on trade with Canada and key to control of Congress in 2026, dislike the Trump administration’s tariffs on the US’s northern neighbor, according to a new poll. The poll by the The Washington Post and Schar School found that most likely voters it surveyed in Michigan, including a majority of independents, weren’t a fan of the tariffs on Canada. Support largely broke down along party lines, with 89 percent of Democrats against them, but only a slim majority – 56 percent – of Republicans in favor. Michigan hosts one of this year’s most closely-watched Senates races, between Republican congressman Mike Rogers, a Republican, and his progressive Democrat challenger Abdul El-Sayed. Unlike other Republicans in northern border states, who have spoken out against the escalating US/Canada trade war, Rogers has largely voiced support for Trump’s tariffs.
